item.content:encoded:
Ol' Shock is a black shuck.

Seeing lines like this is what makes GOI formats so cool. WWS' relationship with the magical world is completely different from the Foundation, and it's always fun to see what they're like when they're operating independently. Sure, he's technically a hell hound, but at heart he's just a good floofy fangpupper.

Also, I'm a fan of this emerging persona of WWS as the one GOI that all the other organizations are pretty much chill with.

item.content:encoded:
This is fantastic. It conflicts with my personal WWS headcanon (a 3Ports location within Tim's reign? I always imagined that they would become that level of competent and engaged only after the take over of Faeowynn Wilson), but since when has that stopped anything from being good? This is a clever interaction between two very different GoIs, which works so very well despite the initial difficulty presented by attempting to mix the two. It is heartwarming, but keeps the grit of the Chicago Spectre, and it's just all very, very good. Bravo.

+1 with gusto.

Also, FINALLY, a NEW WILSON'S FORMAT!! :D been waiting for this and boy howdy you delivered!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Indeed it is! I was inspired when DarkStuff put out that call for alternative formats on the Wilson's Hub discussion page, and was working on this series at the time (which was intended to be entirely GoI-formats until Spirit Stories came along). At one point, I decided that a Wilson's Wildlife format would be one of the more weird choices for a series about anomalous gangsters, but wanted to challenge myself. In any case, it seemed that worked well, since this is one of the higher rated parts of Black as Night already.

item.title: Adoption Poster: Ol' Shock!
item.content:encoded:
This is Part 5 of my ongoing series Black As Night, detailing Mr. Night and the Chicago Spirit/Spectre. You don't need to read the earlier parts, as each part is relatively standalone from the others. This is also totally not an excuse to use a theme I made.

This is also the first Adoption Poster, a new Wilson's Wildlife format. The actual format is the first block of divs, with the emails being an equivalent to addenda on an SCP. It's a somewhat flexible format, with the main bulk of the exposition being able to be delivered in any of three sections (the introduction, the important facts and the foster comments), as you choose. Those sections are also generic enough you can really do anything with them.

The telephone number in this SCP is fake, but the email is not! I set up that gmail for this email, and you are welcome to use it in your own Wilson's articles if you need a generic address. (I don't plan on checking too much/responding in character, though.)

The Endersby Reserve is an in-progress article. I will add a crosslink when it comes out.

Thanks to DrChandra, DarkStuff, and Uncle Nicolini for looking this over in draft form.
